compiled_state.description:
## Summary

A cross-subtree blocking link is silently substituted for library and MCP callers. `rebar link a b depends_on` may record a DIFFERENT edge than the one requested — escalating each endpoint to the nearest common ancestor's children — and the caller is told only `"ok"`.

This is the "Silent" impact bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 reported ("the user believes T1->S was recorded; it was not"). Story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 fixed *which* edge escalation produces, but not whether the caller is told. It remains unfixed on the path agents actually use.

## Root cause

`add_dependency` composes a machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) and prints it to stdout via `_emit_redirect` (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:213`, called at `:269` and `:282`). stdout is the ONLY channel — the record is never returned.

The CLI sees it. Nothing else does:

- `rebar.link()` calls `composer.link_core(..., quiet=True)` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615`);
- `quiet` wraps the call in `contextlib.redirect_stdout(sink), contextlib.redirect_stderr(sink)` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:629`), discarding both the record and the `REDIRECT:` warning;
- the MCP tool `link_tickets` calls `rebar.link(...)` and returns the literal `"ok"` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:213-214`).

So an agent linking two tickets over MCP is told the operation succeeded, with no indication that different endpoints were recorded.

## Approach

Make the redirect record a RETURN VALUE, and leave `quiet=True` alone.

Removing `quiet` is the obvious-looking fix and is wrong: `rebar-mcp` speaks MCP-over-stdio (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:668`), so an unsuppressed `print()` inside a tool call would inject a bare JSON object into the JSON-RPC stream and corrupt the protocol. The same suppression protects the other in-process callers that must not emit stray stdout — the reconciler's inbound apply (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`), `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:106`, and `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:343`. Separately, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py:191` calls `add_dependency` DIRECTLY, bypassing the facade entirely; it ignores the return value, so widening that signature is a no-op for it, but it is listed so the call-site inventory is complete. `quiet` is load-bearing; the defect is that stdout is the only channel, not that it is suppressed.

The propagation chain has FIVE links, and three of them currently drop the value on the floor. Each is named here because the fix silently no-ops if any one is missed:

1. `add_dependency` (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:152`) returns the redirect record, or `None` when nothing was escalated. Its existing stdout print stays exactly as-is, so the CLI contract pinned by `test_add_dependency_cross_story_emits_redirect_json_to_stdout` (`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py:109`) is untouched.
2. `link_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:602`) returns what `add_dependency` returned, still from inside the `quiet` sink.
3. **DROP POINT** — the `_link` inner closure in `rebar.link()` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:614-615`) calls `composer.link_core(...)` with no `return`. Add one.
4. **DROP POINT** — `_python_leaf` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:483`) is annotated `-> None` and calls `fn(*args, repo_root=repo_root, **kwargs)` at `:495` with no `return`. It must return the inner call's value, and its annotation must widen accordingly.
5. **DROP POINT** — `rebar.link()` itself (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:606`) is annotated `-> None`; it must return `_python_leaf`'s value.

Then `link_tickets` returns `"ok"` unchanged when nothing was escalated, and when something was, this exact template:

    ok (escalated: {source}->{target} recorded as {resolved_source}->{resolved_target})

Fixed template rather than free prose, so a consumer can match on it and the test can assert it exactly.

`_python_leaf` is SHARED by every Tier B leaf write (comment, tag, edit, archive, …), so widening it is the one part of this change with reach beyond `link`. It is still safe: those callers ignore the return, so returning a value instead of `None` cannot change their behaviour, and the alternative — bypassing `_python_leaf` for `link` alone — would duplicate its `CommandError -> RebarError` mapping, which is the single thing keeping the library's exit-code contract uniform. Widen the annotation rather than fork the helper.

Rejected: change `link_tickets` to return a structured dict. Better for machine consumption, but it changes the tool's declared return type from `str`, which moves its MCP `outputSchema` and drags in the schema-drift gate (`scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`) and the `tests/interfaces/contracts/` schema guards — a contract change disproportionate to making a substitution visible. Every sibling MUTATE tool (`unlink_tickets`, `edit_ticket`) also returns `"ok"`, so a string keeps the surface consistent. The string is the minimum that removes the silence; a structured payload can follow if a consumer needs to parse it.

Rejected: log a warning instead of returning. `logger.warning` already fires at `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:201` and is swallowed by the same `quiet` sink, so it reaches no one; and a log line is not available to the caller as a value.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — `add_dependency` returns the redirect record (or `None`); the stdout print and its ordering after the durable write are unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` — `link_core` returns what `add_dependency` returned; the `quiet` sink stays.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — THREE edits: the `_link` closure (`:614-615`) returns `link_core`'s value; `_python_leaf` (`:483`) returns its inner `fn(...)` call (`:495`) and widens its `-> None` annotation; `rebar.link()` (`:606`) returns that value and widens its own annotation.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — `link_tickets` reports the substitution in its return string when one occurred.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py` — cover the new return value alongside the existing stdout assertion.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` — cover the MCP tool's two return shapes. If that module does not exist, create it.

## Testing

- Happy path: a sibling link (no escalation) returns `None` from `add_dependency` and `rebar.link()`, and `link_tickets` returns exactly `"ok"` — the unchanged shape.
- Escalation: a cross-subtree link returns a record carrying the original and resolved endpoints, and `link_tickets`' string contains both the requested pair and the recorded pair.
- Regression: the existing stdout assertion still passes, proving the CLI channel was not moved or removed.
- Regression: `quiet=True` still suppresses stdout — asserted by capturing stdout around a `rebar.link()` call that escalates and confirming it is empty, which is the property protecting the MCP stdio stream.
- Edge: a rejected link (redundant / cyclic / closed endpoint) still raises rather than returning a record, so the return value can never be mistaken for success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `add_dependency` returns the redirect record for an escalated link and `None` for an unescalated one; verified by the new cases in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py`.
- [ ] `rebar.link()` returns that same record to library callers; verified by a case asserting the resolved endpoints differ from the requested ones.
- [ ] The MCP `link_tickets` tool returns exactly `"ok"` when nothing was escalated, and exactly `ok (escalated: {source}->{target} recorded as {resolved_source}->{resolved_target})` when something was; verified by the two cases in `tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` asserting the full string, not a substring.
- [ ] `_python_leaf` returns its inner call's value rather than discarding it, and no existing leaf-write caller changes behaviour; verified by a case asserting a non-link leaf write (e.g. `rebar.comment`) still succeeds and by the existing library tests passing unmodified.
- [ ] `rebar.link()` still writes nothing to stdout even when it escalates; verified by capturing stdout around the call and asserting it is empty — the property that keeps the MCP stdio stream intact.
- [ ] `test_add_dependency_cross_story_emits_redirect_json_to_stdout` passes unmodified; verified by `git diff` showing that test body unchanged.
- [ ] The MCP tool's declared return type is still `str`, so `docs/mcp-reference.md` needs no regeneration; verified by `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` leaving the file unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/ tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` all pass; verified by running each.
